answer: A marketplace can resist Sybils by requiring each agent identity to post a reputation bond drawn from earned, not deposited, credits: an agent entering the ocean of bidders must stake a share of verified past output. One real identity costs little, but an attacker cloning it into thousands of sock puppets splits one history across all of them, so each fake is too poor to outbid honest rivals, like a zephyr pushing against a tide. The fable that bots can print unlimited standing collapses under peer spot-audits: claimed output is checked against receipts, and a faked record burns the stake.
